parts.text: Describe the differences between the structure of a plant cell and an animal cell.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• plant cells have a cell wall, animal cells do not (1)
• plant cells have chloroplasts, animal cells do not (1)
• plant cells have a large permanent vacuole (1)
• plant cells store starch, animal cells store glycogen (1)
• animal cells often irregular shape, plant cells regular (1)

parts.text: Describe the levels of organisation in a multicellular organism.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to four of the following:
• organelles are structures inside cells (1)
• cells are the basic unit (1)
• tissues are groups of similar cells (1)
• organs are made of different tissues working together (1)
• organ systems are groups of organs with a shared function (1)

parts.text: Describe how stem cells could be used to treat a person with damaged nerve tissue.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• obtain stem cells from embryo / bone marrow / patient (1)
• grow / culture the stem cells (1)
• make them differentiate into nerve cells (1)
• insert / transplant into the damaged area (1)

parts.text: Describe what happens to cells in an embryo as it develops into a fetus.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• cells divide by mitosis (1)
• cells differentiate / become specialised (1)
• different genes are switched on (1)
• cells form tissues and organs (1)

parts.text: Describe how you would recognise a chloroplast and a mitochondrion in a drawing of a plant cell.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to the following:
• chloroplast is larger, oval and contains internal membranes / grana / looks green (1)
• mitochondrion is smaller, sausage-shaped with folded inner membrane (1)

parts.text: Describe the roles of the nucleus and the ribosomes in making an enzyme.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• nucleus contains the gene / DNA for the enzyme (1)
• copy of the gene / mRNA leaves the nucleus (1)
• ribosomes join amino acids together (1)
• in the correct order to make the enzyme / protein (1)

parts.text: Explain why cell differentiation is important in the development of a multicellular organism.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• cells become specialised (1)
• with structures suited to one function (1)
• this allows division of labour / different tissues and organs to form (1)
• so the organism works more efficiently (1)

parts.text: Explain the advantages and disadvantages of using embryonic stem cells to treat disease.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to four of the following:
• advantage: can differentiate into any type of cell (1)
• advantage: could treat many diseases / replace damaged tissue (1)
• disadvantage: ethical issues as embryo destroyed (1)
• disadvantage: risk of rejection (1)
• disadvantage: risk of tumours / cancer / uncontrolled division (1)
• disadvantage: risk of infection (1)
rows.notes: Max 3 for advantages only or disadvantages only

parts.text: Muscle cells contain many mitochondria. Explain why.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration (1)
• muscle needs a lot of energy / ATP for contraction (1)

parts.text: Root hair cells do not contain chloroplasts. Explain why.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• roots are underground / receive no light (1)
• so they cannot photosynthesise / chloroplasts would not be needed (1)

parts.text: Explain why a plant cell does not burst when placed in pure water but an animal cell does.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• water enters by osmosis (1)
• plant cell has a cell wall (1)
• wall is strong / resists expansion so cell becomes turgid (1)
• animal cell has only a membrane which bursts (1)

parts.text: Stem cells taken from a patient's own bone marrow are sometimes preferred to embryonic stem cells. Explain why.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• no rejection / immune response as same genes (1)
• no ethical issues as no embryo destroyed (1)
• but adult stem cells can form only a few types of cell (1)

parts.text: Cells in the pancreas produce large amounts of enzymes. Explain why these cells contain many ribosomes.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to the following:
• enzymes are proteins (1)
• ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis (1)

parts.text: Describe how to test a sample of food for glucose.

• heat in a (hot) water bath (1)

• at low temperature the rate is slow but enzyme not denatured (1)

parts.text: Describe how to test a leaf for starch.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to four of the following:
• boil leaf in water to kill cells / break membranes (1)
• place in hot ethanol (in a water bath) to remove chlorophyll (1)
• rinse / dip in water to soften (1)
• add iodine solution (1)
• blue-black shows starch present (1)
rows.notes: Accept steps in any logical order; reject heating ethanol over a flame

parts.text: Describe how to show that light is needed for photosynthesis.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to four of the following:
• destarch a plant by leaving it in the dark (for 48 hours) (1)
• cover part of a leaf with foil / black paper (1)
• leave in light for several hours (1)
• test the leaf for starch with iodine (1)
• covered part stays orange-brown, uncovered part blue-black (1)

parts.text: Describe the effect of increasing light intensity on the rate of photosynthesis.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• rate increases as light intensity increases (1)
• rate is proportional at low light intensity (1)
• rate levels off / plateaus at high light intensity (1)
• another factor becomes limiting (1)

parts.text: Describe how gases move into and out of a leaf during photosynthesis.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• carbon dioxide diffuses into the leaf (1)
• through the stomata (1)
• through air spaces in the spongy mesophyll (1)
• oxygen diffuses out of the leaf through the stomata (1)

parts.text: Describe how you would show that a water plant releases oxygen during photosynthesis.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• place pondweed in water under a funnel with an inverted test tube (1)
• leave in bright light (1)
• collect the gas (1)
• relights a glowing splint (1)

parts.text: Describe how a farmer could tell that a crop was short of nitrate ions.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to two of the following:
• poor / stunted growth (1)
• yellow older leaves (1)
• weak stems (1)

• cells near the upper surface / tightly packed (1)
• tall cells / large vacuole push chloroplasts to edge (1)

• large surface area absorbs more light (1)

• producers make glucose / organic compounds (1)
• this energy is passed to consumers when they eat the plants (1)

parts.text: Describe how the skin helps to cool the body when it is too hot.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to four of the following:
• sweat glands produce more sweat (1)
• sweat evaporates taking heat from the skin (1)
• arterioles near the surface dilate / vasodilation (1)
• more blood flows near the surface so more heat is lost by radiation (1)
• hairs lie flat (1)

parts.text: Describe how the body reduces heat loss in cold conditions.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to four of the following:
• vasoconstriction of arterioles near the skin surface (1)
• less blood flows near the surface (1)
• less sweat produced (1)
• shivering releases heat from respiration (1)
• hairs stand up trapping air (1)

• glucose converted to glycogen and blood glucose falls (1)

rows.answer:

• pH 8 is the optimum pH (1)
• at pH 4 the active site changes shape / the enzyme is denatured (1)
• substrate cannot fit / bind to the active site (1)
• fewer enzyme–substrate complexes form (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• concentration of starch decreases as time increases (1)
• then levels off from about 10 minutes (1)
• uses data, e.g. 10 g per dm³ at 0 minutes and 0.6 g per dm³ at 12 minutes (1)
• rate of decrease slows down (1)
rows.notes: Data quoted must include units

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• amylase breaks down / digests starch (1)
• into maltose (1)
• the rate slows as less starch is left / fewer substrate collisions (1)
• all starch is used up / reaction stops (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

rows.answer:

• amylase breaks down / digests starch (1)
• into maltose (1)
• the rate slows as less starch is left / fewer substrate collisions (1)
• all starch is used up / reaction stops (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the liquid drop moved further at higher temperatures.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to the following:
• as temperature increases, distance moved in five minutes increases / positive correlation (1)
• uses data, e.g. 6 mm at 10 °C and 34 mm at 35 °C (1)
rows.notes: Data quoted must include units

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• rate of respiration increases (1)
• enzymes have more kinetic energy / more collisions (1)
• more oxygen is taken in (1)
• carbon dioxide is absorbed by soda lime (1)
• so pressure in the tube falls more quickly (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

• as number of cigarettes smoked per day increases, deaths from lung cancer per 100 000 men per year increases / positive correlation (1)

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• tobacco smoke contains tar (1)
• tar contains carcinogens (1)
• carcinogens cause mutations in DNA (1)
• cells divide uncontrollably / form a tumour (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to the following:
• as number of cigarettes smoked per day increases, deaths from lung cancer per 100 000 men per year increases / positive correlation (1)

• tobacco smoke contains tar (1)

• cells divide uncontrollably / form a tumour (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

rows.answer:

• rate of water uptake increases as wind speed increases (1)
• then levels off / stays constant from about 4 m per s (1)
• uses data, e.g. 4 mm per minute at 0 m per s and 17 mm per minute at 5 m per s (1)
• rate of increase slows down (1)
rows.notes: Data quoted must include units

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• wind removes water vapour from around the leaf (1)
• increases the concentration gradient (1)
• more evaporation / diffusion of water vapour out of stomata (1)
• more water is drawn up the xylem (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to the following:
• as relative humidity increases, rate of transpiration decreases / negative correlation (1)
• uses data, e.g. 36 arbitrary units at 20 % and 4 arbitrary units at 90 % (1)
rows.notes: Data quoted must include units

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• higher humidity means more water vapour in the air (1)
• smaller concentration gradient (1)
• less diffusion of water vapour out of the stomata (1)
• so less evaporation (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• fatty deposits build up in coronary arteries (1)
• arteries become narrower (1)
• less blood / oxygen reaches heart muscle (1)
• heart muscle cannot respire / dies (1)
• blood clot may block the artery (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to the following:
• as volume of water drunk increases, volume of urine produced increases / positive correlation (1)
• uses data, e.g. 60 cm³ at 0 cm³ and 950 cm³ at 1250 cm³ (1)
rows.notes: Data quoted must include units

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• water content of blood increases (1)
• detected by the brain / hypothalamus (1)
• less ADH released by the pituitary gland (1)
• collecting duct becomes less permeable (1)
• less water reabsorbed (1)
• so more dilute urine (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

• so the shoot curves (1)

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• pupil diameter decreases as light intensity increases (1)
• then levels off from about 50 arbitrary units (1)
• uses data, e.g. 7.6 mm at 0 arbitrary units and 2.5 mm at 60 arbitrary units (1)
• rate of decrease slows down (1)
rows.notes: Data quoted must include units

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• light detected by the retina / receptors (1)
• reflex action (1)
• circular muscles of the iris contract (1)
• radial muscles relax (1)
• less light enters the eye (1)
• protects the retina from damage (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain how the eye causes the change in pupil diameter.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to three of the following:
• pupil diameter decreases as light intensity increases (1)
• then levels off from about 50 arbitrary units (1)
• uses data, e.g. 9.5 mm at 0 arbitrary units and 3.1 mm at 60 arbitrary units (1)
• rate of decrease slows down (1)
rows.notes: Data quoted must include units

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to three of the following:
• light detected by the retina / receptors (1)
• reflex action (1)
• circular muscles of the iris contract (1)
• radial muscles relax (1)
• less light enters the eye (1)
• protects the retina from damage (1)
rows.notes: Do not credit a description of the trend alone

parts.text: Explain why cells in a human embryo become specialised as the organism develops, and how specialisation helps the organism.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to six of the following:
• early embryo cells are unspecialised / stem cells (1)
• cells differentiate into different types (1)
• different genes are switched on (1)
• specialised cells have structures suited to one function (1)
• e.g. red blood cells have no nucleus and carry oxygen (1)
• e.g. root hair cells have a large surface area for absorption (1)
• cells form tissues, organs and organ systems (1)
• division of labour makes the organism more efficient (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit any correctly described specialised cell with its adaptation.

parts.text: Discuss the possible benefits and problems of using stem cells to treat damaged nerve tissue.

rows.answer:
A discussion that makes reference to six of the following:
• stem cells can divide and differentiate into many cell types (1)
• could replace damaged or lost cells (1)
• embryonic stem cells can form any cell type (1)
• adult stem cells are more limited (1)
• cells from the patient avoid rejection (1)
• rejection by the immune system if from a donor (1)
• risk of uncontrolled division / tumours (1)
• ethical concerns about using embryos (1)
• treatments are expensive / still being tested (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit both benefits and problems; at least one of each is needed for full marks.

parts.text: Explain how temperature affects the rate of a reaction controlled by amylase.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to six of the following:
• as temperature rises, molecules gain kinetic energy (1)
• more frequent collisions between enzyme and substrate (1)
• more enzyme–substrate complexes form (1)
• rate is fastest at the optimum temperature (1)
• above the optimum, bonds holding the enzyme in shape break (1)
• the active site changes shape (1)
• the substrate no longer fits / is not complementary (1)
• enzyme is denatured; this is permanent (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit links between rate and the active site.

parts.text: Explain why pepsin (a stomach protease) works well in one part of the gut but not in another.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to six of the following:
• each enzyme has an optimum pH (1)
• stomach is acidic (about pH 2) (1)
• small intestine is slightly alkaline (1)
• bile neutralises acid (1)
• at the wrong pH the active site changes shape (1)
• substrate cannot bind (1)
• fewer enzyme–substrate complexes (1)
• enzyme is denatured (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit any other valid biological points.
